Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.

This second bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in case crime No. 169 of 2017, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act, police station Markundi,
District Chitrakoot, with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
The first bail application was dismissed for non prosecution by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 3.12.2021 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 46678 of 2019.

2. Heard learned counsel appearing for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the Rang Lal Mawasi vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184860365/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: entire
record.
None has appeared for informant despite service of notice.
3. It has been argued by learned Counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.

As per first information report, on 15.5.2017 the applicant-accused has called the grand daughter of informant to Chitrakoot and from there he took her to village Kuthla and applicant and co-accused Sarpanch Yadav committed rape upon her.

Learned counsel submitted that alleged incident has been shown of 6.7.2017 but after that no report was lodged and later on an application under Section 156 (3) Cr. P. C. was moved and thereafter this case has been registered on 1.1.2018 in pursuance of the order of the Court.
As per school record, the age of victim is 17 years but as per ossification test report, her age is 18 years and thus, she is a major girl.
Statements of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr. P. C. were referred and it was submitted that her statement and attending facts clearly show that she was a consenting party.

Lastly it was submitted that the applicant is in jail since 11.12.2018 and thus, he has already undergone the detention of more than five years and that trial of the case would take sufficient long time.

The applicant has no criminal antecedent and that in case he is granted bail, he will not misuse liberty of bail and cooperate in the trial.
4.
Learned A. G. A. has opposed the application and submitted that as per school record, victim is a minor girl and she has made allegations of rape against the applicant.

5. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion, the Court is of the view that a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

6. Let the applicant Rang Lal Mawasi involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned subject to the following conditions:
i. The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii.
The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
iii. The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant will not try to contact, threat or otherwise influence the complainant or any of the witness of the case.
7. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel the bail of applicant, in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 14.3.2024 HR  Rang Lal Mawasi vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184860365/
